decision.explanation: The visible evidence does not document progression after the patient reaches 53 years. The available timeline shows prostate adenocarcinoma diagnosis at about 51.98 years, with later imaging and PSA data through about 52.48 years indicating no progression: CT at 52.159 years is reported as showing cancer has not progressed, and MR at 52.483 years has progression recorded as N. PSA also falls from 9.74 to 2.36 to 0.89 ng/mL during that interval. Because the question asks whether cancer will progress in the next 12 months from age 53, the only source-grounded conclusion is that there is no visible evidence of progression in that forward window; therefore the supported MCQ option is No. This is not a prediction of biological certainty, but an evidence-based answer limited to the supplied records.
